title: UK Home Office May Face Investigation Over Use of OpenAI Tech
summary:
A UK government watchdog is considering an investigation into the Home Office’s use of generative AI tools to process asylum applications, WIRED has learned.
The potential probe follows lawmakers and researchers publicly questioning the tools’ accuracy and the government’s secrecy around their use.
They cannot be used in isolation and do not make decisions on claims,” a Home Office spokesperson tells WIRED in an email.
They use the APS as a search assistant to find and summarize country policy information, which informs them whether the applicant faces a genuine risk of harm in their home country.
In July, a UK judge accused the Home Office of citing an “AI hallucinated” document to refuse a Moroccan woman and her child’s asylum claim on the basis that her home country would be safe for her to return to.

title: Massive Groups of Volunteers Are Ready to Face Down ICE at the Polls
summary:
The Franklin County board of elections building at 1700 Morse Street in central Columbus, Ohio, is an early voting site for next week’s midterms.
It is also located in the middle of the large Somali American community that was targeted by the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agency’s Operation Buckeye last December.
The campaign was designed, the agency said, to find “the worst of the worst criminal illegal aliens.”The result was a paltry number of arrests, months of sustained harassment, and a lingering feeling that ICE agents could return at any minute, especially around election time.
They have been trained to document, record, and report any sightings of federal immigration agents, sharing the information in dozens of Signal and WhatsApp groups.
Officially, the Department of Homeland Security has said that it has no plans to deploy ICE agents to polling locations on Election Day.

title: US Supreme Court denies immigration judges the power to shelve deportation cases
summary:
By Andrew ChungOct 27 (Reuters) - The US Supreme Court declined on Tuesday to reinstate the authority of immigration judges to temporarily postpone deportation cases, keeping in place an agreement between President Donald Trump's administration and Republican-governed Texas that bars the once-common practice.
The administration and Texas filed the agreement in a federal court in Texas on June 22, the same day that the state sued to challenge the immigration court procedure.

title: Israeli military detains Egyptian national who crossed border
summary:
Egyptian man held after crossing into Israel near Nitzana, his motive for the crossing still unknown.
Israel’s military has said that it detained an Egyptian civilian overnight after he crossed a border fence from Egyptian territory into Israel near Nitzana and that he was transferred to security forces for further questioning.
Nitzana is a small community in southern Israel’s western Negev (Naqab) Desert, sitting directly adjacent to the Egyptian border opposite the Egyptian side’s Al-Awja area.
The Nitzana border crossing, also known as the Eliav crossing, primarily handles cargo transport between the two countries rather than serving as a major passenger channel.
The incident occurred as Israel maintains heightened alert levels along the Egyptian border.
